label: November 1918
headline: The Guns Fall Silent
deck: Germany signs the armistice in the forest of Compiègne; the Kaiser goes into exile
caption: Sailors of the High Seas Fleet march under red flags along the quays of Kiel
body: Ordered to sea for a last battle, the sailors of the High Seas Fleet refuse. On 3 November the mutiny reaches Kiel, and within days councils of soldiers and workers hold the cities of Germany. On 9 November the Kaiser's abdication is announced and a republic is proclaimed from the Reichstag; the next day he crosses into Holland.

In a railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne a German delegation signs Marshal Foch's terms at five in the morning of 11 November. At eleven o'clock the guns fall silent along the whole front; Canadian troops have entered Mons that morning.
Austria-Hungary signed its armistice on 3 November and is breaking into new nations.
briefs: The German fleet steams into the Firth of Forth to be interned
Poland declares its independence under Józef Piłsudski
Lettow-Vorbeck surrenders in East Africa, the last German force in the field
